directAnswer: To update USB-C charging capabilities on your laptop, ensure your firmware and drivers are up to date, and verify compatibility with your USB-C charger.
summary: Updating USB-C charging on a laptop involves checking for firmware updates and ensuring charger compatibility.

sections.heading: Check for Firmware Updates
sections.body: Access your laptop's settings to check for firmware updates. This can usually be found under 'System' or 'About' sections, depending on your operating system.

sections.heading: Update USB Drivers
sections.body: Ensure that your USB drivers are up to date. This can typically be done through the Device Manager on Windows or System Preferences on macOS.

sections.heading: Verify Charger Compatibility
sections.body: Use a USB-C / charger compatibility checker tool to confirm that your charger meets the power requirements of your laptop.

steps.title: Windows Firmware Update
steps.detail: Go to 'Settings' > 'Update & Security' > 'Windows Update' and check for updates.

steps.title: macOS Firmware Update
steps.detail: Click on the Apple menu > 'About This Mac' > 'Software Update' to check for updates.

steps.title: Update USB Drivers on Windows
steps.detail: Open 'Device Manager', expand 'Universal Serial Bus controllers', right-click on each USB device, and select 'Update driver'.

steps.title: Update USB Drivers on macOS
steps.detail: Drivers are updated with macOS updates; ensure your macOS is current.

faqs.question: What if my laptop doesn't support USB-C charging?
faqs.answer: Check the laptop specifications or user manual to confirm if USB-C charging is supported.

faqs.question: Can I use any USB-C charger?
faqs.answer: Not all USB-C chargers are compatible; ensure the charger meets the wattage requirements of your laptop.

faqs.question: How do I know if my firmware is up to date?
faqs.answer: Most operating systems will notify you of available firmware updates; you can also check the manufacturer's website for the latest versions.

caveats: Not all laptops support USB-C charging; check your laptop's specifications.
Using an incompatible charger may lead to slow charging or damage.
